stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

The clerk did not received the letter until Monday.
hints: Look at the helping verb "did". What form should the main verb after it take?
"Did" already shows that the action is in the past. Should the verb after it show the past again?
After did, do or does, use the plain form of the verb, with no -ed and no -s. Check the verb after "did not", then check the other parts.

solution.methodName: Use the plain verb after did, do or does

steps.why: A helping verb is a small verb such as do, does, did, has or will that comes before the main verb.

steps.action: "Did" already shows the past, so the main verb must be in its plain form: "receive".
steps.why: English shows the past only once. "Did not received" shows it twice. The plain form is the one you find in the dictionary.

steps.action: Check the other parts. "the letter" and "until Monday" are correct.
The error is "did not received". It should be "did not receive".

trapNotes.the letter: This part is correct. It names the thing that was received.
trapNotes.until Monday: This part is correct. "Until Monday" means the letter arrived only on Monday.
trapNotes.No error: The sentence is about the past, so "received" may feel right. But after "did", the verb goes back to its plain form: "did not receive".
